CT-URFX-COVER/.5H

My initial intention with the Basin Style SKUs was not to include the material + color suffix in the code, but I was not accounting for the added group layer from Porcelain (stone vs marble). How might we use the approach I've displayed above in this context?
Reply:
	Hi @ryan@hastingsbath.com



We need to pass on the material code if it is an exception, such as POR, to understand what kind of material it is and which group it belongs to.
We see this implementation.
Your example as a result of CT-URFX-COVER/.5H is quite suitable for SKUs without exceptions. 

For exceptions where there is a dependence on the material, we offer the option CT-URPOR-COVER/.5H-CT-POR-TR2, which will be more universal, because we preserve the structure of the material -CT-POR-TR2 everywhere.
Another option we can consider is shortening it to -POR-TR2, which would result in CT-URPOR-COVER/.5H-POR-TR2, with fewer duplicates but a universal approach to parsing material in SKUs, without exceptions.

This will create an exception for material recognition and parsing.
In our opinion, the CT-URPOR-COVER/.5H-CT-POR-TR2 option is more versatile because we keep the -CT-POR-TR2 structure everywhere.
We can also shorten it to -POR-TR2, resulting in CT-URPOR-COVER/.5H-POR-TR2, fewer duplicates.

Therefore, our option is to provide a pricing scheme for working with short SKUs without material and with material. 
The pricing system will support 2 SKUs at the input 
CT-URFX-COVER/.5H - if there is no need
CT-URPOR-COVER/.5H-POR-TR2 - if there is a separation as in porcelain
